meta.title: Features
meta.description: Every BinPar feature, grouped: visible evidence, clinical consultation, answer formats, personal workspace and institutional governance.

evidence.title: Visible evidence
evidence.heading: Visible
evidence.lead: Every statement points to the document that supports it. You read the passage in context, with its provenance and currency in view.

consultation.title: Clinical consultation
consultation.heading: Clinical
consultation.lead: You put the question as you would at a clinical meeting. Each specialty reviews its corpus, progress stays in view and the conversation keeps the case.

formats.title: Answer formats
formats.heading: Answer
formats.lead: The answer comes in the format that explains it best. Diagrams, figures and tables keep their citations and open in the side panel.

workspace.title: Personal workspace
workspace.heading: Personal
workspace.lead: Each professional organises their queries into projects with their own instructions and sources, and adjusts how answers read.

governance.title: Institutional governance
governance.heading: Institutional
governance.lead: The organisation decides which documents the committee consults, reviews every change before publishing it and checks that answer quality holds.

citations.title: Citations per statement
citations.description: Every statement links to its source.
citations.detail: Click the number next to a sentence and the supporting document opens, with the answer still in view.

bibliography.title: References
bibliography.description: The sources used, at the end of every answer.
bibliography.detail: The list gathers the guidelines and manuals cited, so you can see at a glance which documents each answer rests on.

preserved.title: Preserved evidence
preserved.description: The answer keeps what it cited, even if the document is withdrawn.
preserved.detail: If a guideline is withdrawn or replaced, the cited passage stays available, so you can review what that answer was based on.

viewer.title: Document viewer
viewer.description: The PDF, open at the cited page with the passage highlighted.
viewer.detail: The original document opens in a side panel, so you read the passage in context, with what comes before and after it.

verified.title: Verified text
verified.description: Shows whether the passage matches the original PDF.
verified.detail: The cited text is checked against the source document, and an indicator shows whether it matches the PDF word for word.

provenance.title: Full provenance
provenance.detail: Every citation keeps its exact location in the document, so you can find it or refer to it at a clinical meeting or in a report.

updates.title: Update notices
updates.description: Flags data superseded by a later source.
updates.detail: When a newer edition changes the cited information, a notice next to the passage says so, so you can check it is still current.

natural.title: Natural language
natural.description: You put the question as you would at a clinical meeting.
natural.detail: You describe the case with its history, medication and what concerns you, with no keywords or forms.

clarify.title: Clarifying questions
clarify.description: If a key detail is missing, the committee asks for it.
clarify.detail: When the answer depends on a value you have not given, such as the glomerular filtration rate, the question comes before the answer, with options to reply in one click.

followup.title: Follow-up
followup.detail: A new question builds on the case and the sources already consulted, without repeating the patient's details.

committee.title: Committee by specialty
committee.description: Several experts, each with its own corpus.
committee.detail: Each specialty reviews the documents in its field, and the answer brings together and contrasts their contributions.

modes.title: Answer modes
modes.description: Speed or depth, for every question.
modes.detail: Each organisation defines its answer modes; when there is more than one, the professional chooses next to the query box between a quick answer and a more thorough review.

progress.title: Visible progress
progress.description: Experts, sources and pages consulted, while the answer is prepared.
progress.detail: While you wait, you can see which specialties are working, which documents they are reviewing and on which pages, before you read the answer.

images.title: Attached images
images.description: Pasted, dragged or attached to the query.
images.detail: An ECG, a set of lab results or a photographed lesion can be added to the question and consulted alongside the case.

schemes.title: Clinical diagrams
schemes.description: Decision trees and mind maps, with sources.
schemes.detail: A decision tree lays out the criteria behind the answer, and every diagram shows the sources it rests on.

figures.title: Corpus figures
figures.description: Figures from the guidelines, inside the answer.
figures.detail: When a guideline includes a relevant illustration, the figure appears next to the text that explains it.

download.title: Download as image
download.description: Every diagram exports as a PNG.
download.detail: Save the diagram as an image to use in a clinical meeting, a protocol or teaching material.

tables.title: Comparison tables
tables.detail: Drugs, criteria or alternatives are compared in columns, and every row keeps the reference to its document.

textalt.title: Text walkthrough
textalt.description: An accessible alternative to every diagram.
textalt.detail: Every diagram can be read as a list of steps, useful with screen readers or for copying into a report.

panel.title: Side panel
panel.description: Documents, diagrams and images in tabs.
panel.detail: Sources, diagrams and figures open next to the conversation, with the answer still in view.

projects.title: Projects
projects.detail: Queries on the same matter, such as a protocol review, sit together in one space with their own instructions and sources.

instructions.title: Shared instructions
instructions.description: Format, language or approach for a whole project.
instructions.detail: You state once how the project's answers should be presented; clinical rules and institutional sources keep their priority.

saved.title: Answers as sources
saved.description: Save an answer for the rest of the project.
saved.detail: A final answer is saved as a private source and can be retrieved from other conversations in the same project.

preferences.title: Answer preferences
preferences.description: Length, tone and format, remembered across chats.
preferences.detail: Preferences are stored and apply to every chat; they adjust the presentation, not the purpose or the clinical rules.

private.title: Private documents
private.description: PDF, TXT and Markdown, citable as sources.
private.detail: A department protocol or your own notes are added to the project and cited like any other source, visible only to their owner.

history.title: Organised history
history.description: Pin, rename, move and jump by question.
history.detail: Conversations can be pinned, renamed or moved to a project, and in longer ones you can jump straight to each question.

languages.title: Three languages
languages.detail: The interface appears in the language each professional chooses, and the change applies instantly.

theme.title: Light and dark theme
theme.description: Comfortable reading in clinic or on call.
theme.detail: Dark mode reduces glare on night shifts, and light mode makes reading easier in clinic lighting.

corpus.title: Corpus per organisation
corpus.description: Your own protocols on a shared base.
corpus.detail: The centre's protocols are added on top of a shared base of guidelines and manuals, and the committee consults both with the same traceability.

library.title: Document library
library.description: An inventory of the guidelines, with type and summary.
library.detail: Each document is listed with its type, approval date, the experts it feeds and a summary of what it contributes.

committees.title: Configurable committees
committees.description: Experts and modes defined per organisation.
committees.detail: Each organisation configures its committee's answer modes and sets one as the default; when there is more than one, the professional chooses between them in the chat.

review.title: Review before publication
review.description: Changes are reviewed before they enter the corpus.
review.detail: A new document or an update is reviewed and approved before it is published, so nothing reaches the answers unchecked.

versions.title: Corpus versions
versions.description: Every change is logged and versioned.
versions.detail: The corpus keeps its history: what changed, when and in which documents, so you can reconstruct what each answer was based on.

control.title: Control questions
control.description: Question sets that detect whether answers degrade.
control.detail: A set of questions with reference answers is rerun after every change and flags those that get worse compared with the previous version.

rating.title: Professional feedback
rating.description: Useful or not useful, with a comment for review.
rating.detail: Each professional marks an answer as useful or not useful and adds a comment, which goes to the editorial team for review.

brand.title: Your own brand and domain
brand.detail: The platform appears with the organisation's logo, colours and domain.

features.

intro.lead: What is worth checking before you bring it to your organisation: where each answer comes from, who decides which documents it consults and how its quality is monitored over time.
